filled with chlorine gas. The molecular equation for this reaction is;
Na+ Cl2
NaCl
Thus, the half-reaction is;
Na
Na+ + e- [Sodium metal oxidised to sodium ion]
2e- + Cl2
2Cl- [chlorine molecule is reduced to chloride ion]
In this reaction, sodium oxidizes chlorine, so it is a reducing agent
whereas chlorine reduces sodium, so is an oxidising agent.

The substance that itself is oxidised helps in the reduction of others is called reducing agent or reductant. The substance that itself is reduced and helps in the oxidation of others is called oxidising agent or oxidant.

6.2 Oxidation number and rules for assigning oxidation number Activity:
Observe the part of the periodic table where certain numbers are given in each group except for group 1 and 18. Identify the numbers for these groups.

During the redox reactions, electrons are lost as well as gained by the atoms. Certain numbers are used to describe the degree of loss or gain of electrons in such reactions. These numbers areoxidation numbers. The oxidation number of an atom in a molecule or ion is the charge that an atom would have if all electrons in its bonds were assigned to the more electronegative atom. The following simple conventions are useful to calculate the oxidation number of each atom in a molecule or ion:
a. Oxidation number of atoms in free state or elemental form is zero. For example, the oxidation number of chlorines in Cl2, phosphorous in P4 or iron in Fe is 0.
b. Certain elements have same oxidation number in almost all their compounds: i. Fluorine always has oxidation number of -1. ii. Group 1 elements forming +1 ions (Li+, Na+, K+) oxidation number =0.
iii. Group 2 always forms +2 ions: Mg2+, Ca2+, etc. oxidation number =+2. c. Oxidation number of hydrogens is +1 in covalent compounds but -1 in ionic compounds(hydrides).
For examples: covalent compounds (H2O, NH3, CH4) oxidation number of H =+1 ionic compounds (NaH, LiH, CaH2) oxidation number of H =-1
d. Oxidation number of oxygens is -2 in normal oxides, but is -1 and -1/2 is peroxides and superoxides respectively.
Examples: Normal oxides (NO, CO2, P2O5), oxidation number of oxygen =-2 CHEMISTRY, GRADE 11 | 219
Peroxides (H2O2, Na2O2) oxidation number of oxygen =-1 Super oxides (KO2, NaO2) oxidation number of oxygen =-1/2

In the case of molecule of nonmetals, more electronegative atom carries negative oxidation number whereas less electronegative atom carries positive oxidation number.
ClO2 oxidation number of oxygen is -2 and that of chlorine is +7 because Oxygen is more electronegative than chlorine.
ICl3 oxidation number of -1 and that of Iodine is +3 because chlorine is more electronegative than iodine.
